+# How often a FileSystemLoader looks at its search paths for changes, in
+# seconds. Polling is slower to notice than the operating system's own
+# notifications, but it needs nothing beyond the standard library and
+# behaves the same on every platform.
+_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.5
+
+_Fingerprint = t.Tuple[int, int, int]
+
+
+def _snapshot_files(
+    searchpaths: t.Iterable[str], followlinks: bool
+) -> t.Dict[str, _Fingerprint]:
+    """Map the absolute path of every file below the search paths to a
+    cheap fingerprint of it. Two snapshots differ at a path when the
+    file was added, removed or rewritten in between.
+    """
+    found: t.Dict[str, _Fingerprint] = {}
+
+    for searchpath in searchpaths:
+        for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(searchpath, followlinks=followlinks):
+            for filename in filenames:
+                path = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
+
+                try:
+                    stat = os.stat(path)
+                except OSError:
+                    # Gone since the directory was listed, or a broken
+                    # link. Either way it is not a template right now.
+                    continue
+
+                found[os.path.abspath(path)] = (
+                    stat.st_mtime_ns,
+                    stat.st_size,
+                    stat.st_ino,
+                )
+
+    return found
+
+
+def _relative_pieces(path: str, base: str) -> t.Optional[t.Tuple[str, ...]]:
+    """The segments of ``path`` below the directory ``base``, or ``None``
+    if ``path`` is not below it. Both must be absolute. Nothing is read
+    from the file system, so a file that was deleted works too.
+    """
+    try:
+        relative = os.path.relpath(path, base)
+    except ValueError:
+        # Different drives on Windows.
+        return None
+
+    pieces = tuple(relative.split(os.path.sep))
+
+    if pieces[0] in (os.path.curdir, os.path.pardir) or os.path.isabs(relative):
+        return None
+
+    return pieces
+
+
+def _watch_search_paths(
+    loader_ref: "weakref.ref[FileSystemLoader]", stop: threading.Event
+) -> None:
+    """Body of the monitoring thread of one :class:`FileSystemLoader`.
+
+    The thread only holds a weak reference to the loader, so watching a
+    loader never keeps it, or the environments it serves, alive. It ends
+    when the loader is collected, when ``stop`` is set, or when the
+    loader reports that there is nothing left to watch for.
+    """
+    while not stop.wait(_POLL_INTERVAL):
+        loader = loader_ref()
+
+        if loader is None or not loader._poll_search_paths():
+            return
+
+        # Do not hold the loader while waiting for the next round.
+        del loader
+
